observed_title: Fractional harmonic measure in minimum Riesz energy problems with external fields
version: Local 24-page manuscript; source text states the Riesz variational problem and theorems, publication metadata not independently checked.

read_ranges.scope: 逐页阅读全文及参考文献，PDF p.1–24 / paper.md L1–1302；证明链、附录（若有）均纳入阅读。

topic_relevance.legacy-iterated-compensating-measure: direct only for the article’s own Riesz external-field minimization and threshold; adjacent as a warning that existence is conditional, with no interface matching the private iterated-compensator notation.

definitions.name: Inner α-harmonic sweep
definitions.statement: ε_z^A=(ε_z)_A is the inner α-Riesz sweep; H_z:=1/ε_z^A(R^n)≥1. Depending on thinness at infinity, H_z=1 or 1/U_{γ_A}(z) in the extended equilibrium-measure sense.

definitions.name: External field
definitions.statement: f_{q,z}(y)=−q|y−z|^(α−n); the admissible class consists of probability measures on A with finite energy under the paper’s assumptions.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.1: existence threshold for the Gauss minimizer
assumptions: Riesz kernel κα(x,y)=|x−y|^(α−n), n≥2, 0<α≤2, α<n; the paper’s standing Q and energy setup.
Closedness condition (P) on the cone of positive finite-energy measures on A; z∈A_u∪A^c; external field f_{q,z}=−q|·−z|^(α−n).
theorem_cards.statement: The minimizer λ_{A,f_{q,z}} exists iff c*(A)<∞ or q≥H_z, where H_z=1/ε_z^A(R^n) from the inner α-harmonic sweep. If c*(A)=∞, the solvable q set is [H_z,∞); if finite, it is all positive q.
proof_steps: For finite outer capacity, strong completeness of the admissible cone ensures the extremal measure has unit mass, so it is the minimizer.
At q=H_z, H_z ε_z^A has unit mass and attains the infimum.
For q>H_z, compare the extremal potential with qU_{ε_z^A}; positivity of mass rules out a nonnegative weighted constant, forcing extremal mass 1.

For c*(A)=∞ and q<H_z, choose small-energy measures escaping to infinity, perturb qε_z^A by them to construct a minimizing net whose vague limit has mass q/H_z<1; hence the extremal measure is not a probability minimizer.
gaps: Uses prior potential-theoretic results: strong completeness, positivity of mass, balayage identities, and extremal-measure lemmas are cited from the paper’s reference framework.
The theorem is not a general theorem about “compensating measures”; its conclusion belongs to this Riesz variational problem.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.10: alternative representations and support behavior of the minimizer
assumptions: Theorem 2.10 standing hypotheses, including (P), z∈A_u∪A^c, α-Riesz energy setup, and a regime in which Theorem 2.1 gives existence.
For subthreshold q<H_z the finite-capacity branch c*(A)<∞ is necessary.
theorem_cards.statement: At q=H_z the minimizer is H_z ε_z^A. At q<H_z with finite capacity, it is qε_z^A + ((H_z−q)/(H_z c*(A)))γ_A, with the paper’s inner equilibrium measure γ_A. The proof obtains the representation via weighted equilibrium and balayage identities; support conclusions are stated separately in Theorem 2.12.
proof_steps: At threshold, invoke Theorem 2.1’s formula and the weighted equilibrium characterization to identify the unique minimizer.
Below threshold with finite capacity, define δ=qε_z^A+Lγ_A, L=(H_z−q)/(H_zc*(A)); its mass is one and potential is constant on A quasi-everywhere.
Compare with the variational characterization to identify δ as λ and its weighted constant.
Represent λ as a sweep of qε_z+cγ_A using idempotence/linearity properties of sweep.
The no-compensation observation in Remark 2.2 follows only for closed A, z∈A_u, and solvable q; it says the variational infimum is attained, not that the added measure is useless.
gaps: Potential identities and uniqueness are supported by cited Theorem 3.3/3.6 and balayage results; the article invokes these rather than reproving all foundations.
Support compactness/noncompactness is in Theorem 2.12, not a consequence of the mass-threshold statement alone.

constant_dependence.explicit: The threshold is H_z=1/ε_z^A(R^n); subthreshold representation uses L=(H_z−q)/(H_z c*(A)). No concentration inequality is asserted.

endpoint_limits.existence: Theorem 2.1 requires (P) and z∈A_u∪A^c; finite capacity makes every q>0 solvable, infinite capacity yields q≥H_z.
endpoint_limits.compensation: No-compensation remark is restricted to closed A and z∈A_u in the solvable regime; it is not a general claim for signed measures.
endpoint_limits.capacity: If q<H_z and c*(A)=∞, the solution does not exist.

reusable_methods.method: Threshold a variational existence question by the mass of an inner sweep
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires the same Riesz kernel, conductor-supported energy class, and sweep/potential theory; it cannot be transferred to arbitrary jump compensation.

reusable_methods.method: Use escaping finite-energy perturbations to test whether a minimizing net has unit mass
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires an escape-to-infinity sequence with vanishing energy and control of vague limits.
